# Germany's BASF lifts profit outlook again as Iran war disruptions support demand

By Tristan Veyet

Oct 28 (Reuters) - German chemicals group BASF raised its 2026 outlook for the second time this year after its third-quarter core earnings topped market expectations on Wednesday, as European chemical suppliers benefit from an Iran war-related demand boost.

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has been an unexpected boon for German chemical businesses, as Middle East supply disruptions drove up local demand, bolstering the struggling sector even as energy prices soared.

BASF said it expected adjusted core earnings to land between €7.4 billion and €7.8 billion ($8.2 billion and $8.7 billion) this year, up from the range of €6.9 billion to €7.7 billion it had given in July.

# BASF beats expectations and raises full-year targets

Published on 10/28/2026 at 12:21 pm IST - Modified on 10/28/2026 at 01:03 pm IST

Reuters - Translated by Marketscreener
...
Chemicals group BASF unexpectedly increased its earnings significantly in the third quarter, helped by higher prices and a slight increase in volumes. Adjusted operating profit (EBITDA) rose 15 percent to €1.64bn, the Ludwigshafen-based company said Wednesday. BASF thus exceeded analysts' expectations of €1.495bn on average. Revenue climbed 14 percent to just under €16.4bn. In light of strong performance in its core businesses, the group raised its full-year targets again: For 2026, BASF now expects adjusted earnings of between €7.4bn and €7.8bn, after previously forecasting €6.9bn to €7.7bn.
